newsitem.title: USA: Ryerson Tull says to acquire Thypin Steel.
newsitem.headline: Ryerson Tull says to acquire Thypin Steel.

text.p: Ryerson Tull Inc said it signed a definitive agreement to buy Thypin Steel Co Inc, a privately held distributor and processor of carbon and stainless steel products, for about $120 million in cash.
Ryerson said it will purchase all outstanding stock of Thypin and assume about $20 million in existing Thypin debt.
Based in New York, Thypin has seven locations and annual sales of approximately $335 million.
The transaction is expected to close in early 1997, said Ryerson, a metal processor and distributor.
"We expect the transaction to be additive to Ryerson Tull's 1997 earnings," said Ryerson chief executive Neil Novich.
The acquired operation will continue to use the Thypin name in its marketplace and be operated as part of the Ryerson East business unit, the company said.
Ryerson Tull completed an initial public offering of 13 percent of its common stock in June 1996. The remaining 87 percent of the stock is owned by Inland Steel Industries Inc .
